scope: All six Table 4 pastes (two metakaolins, each plain, with SiC nanowhiskers or with CNTs) with the shared batch masses and molar ratios. Rheology and strength results are plotted only in figures, so no per-mix results are transcribed.
madeBy: AI transcription · mix-sheet skill v1 (source-text pilot)

materials.name: MK1
materials.detail: The metakaolin MK1 was obtained calcinating kaolin at 800 °C for 1 h (KK260, Linn Elektro Therm GmbH, Bad Frankenhausen, Germany) in a static muffle.

materials.name: MK2
materials.detail: The metakaolin MK2, a commercial product, was provided by a local industrial company.

materials.name: sodium silicate solution
materials.detail: The alkaline activator was prepared with sodium silicate solution (Na2SiO3–H2O), with SiO2/Na2O = 3.37, and sodium hydroxide—NaOH (micro pellets) (≥98% purity).

materials.name: NaOH micro pellets
materials.detail: Briefly, the NaOH micro pellets were dissolved in a sodium silicate solution using a magnetic stirrer.

cures.text: Subsequently, all samples were sealed with plastic films and cured at 23 ± 2 °C. The samples were kept at ambient temperature until the day of the tests.

gaps: Table quotes follow the standard form; the mix names are Table 4's own ("R1 (MK1 + AS)", "R2 + NW", …). "NW" in Table 4 is the SiC whisker addition called SCW in the text; 0.20 g of addition per 100 g MK is from Table 4.

"HS" (8.9 g) is not defined in the paper; it is read as the NaOH from the methods ("NaOH micro pellets were dissolved in a sodium silicate solution"). The 100.0 g MK is attributed to MK1 for R1 rows and MK2 for R2 rows per the mix names.

Batch masses (100.0 g MK, 120.0 g sodium silicate, 8.9 g NaOH) are stated once for all mixtures in §2.6; the review note's question on the NaOH physical form is answered: micro pellets dissolved in the silicate.
Yield stress, viscosity and compressive strength are only in figures; Na2O/SiO2 (Table 4) has no parameter key.
